text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Some 269,700 people, 10.5 percent of the workforce, were unemployed in the third quarter of this year. The unemployment rate was 0.8 percent lower than in the previous quarter.
- The paper quotes unnamed sources from the ruling coalition as saying the government was considering replacing the finance and agriculture ministers within the next few weeks.
- Parliament on Tuesday dismissed Jozef Darmo, general director of the official Slovak Television, and replaced him with Igor Kubis.

- Whirlpool Slovakia said it planned to double production of washing machines to some 266,000 units this year. The company said next year's output should be some 291,000 units, and that exports should account for about 90 percent of overall production.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The average nominal wage in industry rose by 13.9 percent year-on-year in the first nine months of this year to 8,185 crowns.
- The Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) said it would call on the governemnt to adopt a long-term economic policy which should ensure further decrease in the unemployment rate.
- The central Slovak town of Banska Bystrica will issue a 150 million crown tranche of 10-year bonds with a fixed, annual coupon of 10 percent and a nominal value of 100,000 crowns.
- The Organisation for Economic Development, an independent economic think-tank, warned that foreign investors could turn away from Slovakia due to the lack of democracy in the country.
- Telecomunication equipment producer Tesla a.s. will supply state-run telecom monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie with digital exchanges worth 400 million crowns over the next four years.
